senses.gloss:
वृत, अस्, आ, अम्, surrounded, covered, screened,
defended; chosen, selected; hired; preferred; agreed,
assented to; served; affected by; vitiated, spoiled;
(अम्), n., Ved. a treasure, wealth (according to
Naigh. II. 10).
—वृत-पत्त्रा, f. a kind of plant
(= पुत्र-दात्री).

1. वृत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, turned; round, rounded,
circular; been, existed, lived; happened, (किं-
वृत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, ‘one who says to himself, What
has happened?’ one who allows himself to be taken
by surprise, incautious); occurred, past, gone, finished;
dead, deceased; done, performed, acted, engaged in,
undertaken; proceeded, proceeding from, derived
from; read through, studied; fixed, firm; unim-
paired; famous; (अस्), m. a tortoise; (आ), f. a kind
of tree or shrub (= झिञ्झिरिष्टा); (अम्), n. a
circle, circumference; (in astronomy) the epicycle
(= परिधि); event, occurrence, news; procedure;
practice, profession, occupation, mode of life, means
of subsistence; act, action, behaviour, manner, de-
meanour, (उज्झित-धैर्य-वृत्तम्, without regard
to dignity of manner); conduct; observance of any
enjoined practice, established rule or usage, actual
practice, law; ‘the turn of a line,’ final rhythm,
rhythm; verse, metre.
—वृत्त-कर्कटी, f. the
water-melon (= षड्-भुजा).
—वृत्त-खण्ड,
[]
अम्, n. a portion or segment of a circle.
—वृत्त-
गन्धि, इस्, इस्, इ, having only the smell of verse or
rhythm; (इ), n. epithet of a particular kind of
prose.
—वृत्त-गुण्ड, अस्, m. a kind of grass (=
दीर्घ-नाल).
—वृत्त-चूड or वृत्त-चौल, अस्,
आ, अम्, whose tonsure has been performed, tonsured,
(this should be performed at the age of one or three
years, cf. Manu II. 35.)
—वृत्त-ज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्,
knowing actions or established practices.
—वृत्त-
तण्डुल, अस्, m. a sort of grass (= यव-नाल).
—वृत्त-तस्, ind. according to the practice or ob-
servance of caste, according to usage or customary
procedure, (वृत्ततः पापम्, a sin according to
caste.)
—वृत्त-निष्पाविका, f. a kind of leguminous
plant (= नख-निष्पावी).
—वृत्त-पर्णी, f. a
kind of plant (= पाठा).
—वृत्त-पुष्प, अस्, m. the
Śirīṣa tree; the Kadamba; = वानीर; = कुब्जक;
= मुद्गर.
—वृत्त-प्रत्यभिज्ञ, अस्, आ, अम्,
well versed in sacred rites.
—वृत्त-फल, अस्, m.
the pomegranate (= दाडिम); the jujube; (आ), f.,
N. of various plants, = वार्ताकी, = शशाण्डुली, =
आमलकी; (अम्), n. black pepper.
—वृत्त-बाहु,
उस्, उस्, उ, round-armed, (see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 67.)
—वृत्त-मल्लिका, f. a species of plant (= मोदिनी,
= श्वेतार्क).
—वृत्त-यमक, अम्, n. a kind of
verse containing a play on words, (see यमक.)
—वृत्त-रत्नाकर (˚न-आक्˚), अस्, m. ‘ocean of
metres,’ N. of a short metrical treatise on Post-vedic
metres by Kedāra.
—वृत्त-रत्नाकर-टीका, f. and
वृत्त-रत्नाकर-सेतु, उस्, m., N. of two commen-
taries on the above-mentioned work.
—वृत्त-वत्,
आन्, अती, अत्, one who has performed the duties of
caste or calling, well-conducted.
—वृत्त-वीज, अस्,
m. a kind of plant, = भिण्डा; (आ), f. another plant,
= आढकी.
—वृत्त-वीजका, f. a kind of plant, =
पाण्डुर-फली.
—वृत्त-शत, अम्, n., N. of a work
mentioned in the Śūdra-dharma-tattva.
—वृत्त-
शस्त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, one who has studied (the
science of) arms or warfare (= अधीत-शस्त्रविद्य,
Bhaṭṭi-k. IX. 19).
—वृत्त-सम्पन्न, अस्, आ, अम्,
well behaved or conducted, behaving with propriety.
—वृत्त-सादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, destroying established
usage, worthless, mean, vile.
—वृत्त-स्थ, अस्, आ,
अम्, abiding in the duties of caste or calling.
—वृत्-
ताध्ययनर्द्धि (˚त-अध्˚, ˚न-ऋद्˚), इस्, f. in-
crease of moral conduct and study, holiness resulting
from observance of rules and study (of scripture).
—वृत्तानुवर्तिन् (˚त-अन्˚), ई, इनी, इ, conforming
to rule, obedient.
—वृत्तानुसार (˚त-अन्˚), अस्,
m. conforming to prescribed practice; conformity
to metre; (आत्), ind. according to the metre or
measure of a verse, for the sake of the metre.
—वृत्तानुसारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, conforming to established
rule or practice, doing what is enjoined or proper.
—वृत्तान्त (˚त-अन्˚), अस्, m., (rarely) अम्, n. ‘the
end or result of a course of action,’ occurrence, inci-
dent, event; tidings, rumour, report, intelligence;
a tale, story, narrative, history, account; an ancient
story; topic, subject; sort, kind, difference; mode,
manner, state, condition; interval, rest, leisure, op-
portunity; property, nature; the whole, totality;
alone, solitary.
—वृत्तान्त-दर्शिन्, ई, इनी, इ, wit-
nessing or being a spectator of any action.
—वृत्-
तान्तान्वेषक (˚त-अन्˚), अस्, इका, अम्, inquiring into
what takes place.
—वृत्तेर्वारु (˚त-इर्˚), उस्, m. a
water-melon (= षड्-भुजा).
—वृत्तोरु (˚त-ऊरु),
उस्, f. a round-thighed woman, (see Pāṇ. IV. 1, 69.)
—वृत्तौजस् (˚त-ओज्˚), आस्, आस्, अस्, having unim-
paired power, whose (creative) energy had free and
unobstructed course, (Manu 1. 6); of great energy,
mighty, irresistible.

2. वृत्त, अस्, आ, अम् (perhaps incorrect for वृत),
chosen, selected, appointed, &c.

वृति, इस्, f. surrounding, encompassing; hiding,
secreting; an enclosure, hedge, fence, an enclosed
piece of ground or place enclosed for particular culti-
vation (especially that of the Piper Betel, which in
many parts of India is surrounded and screened by
mats); selecting, choosing, preferring, appointing;
a selection, choice, soliciting, asking, requesting; a
request.
—वृतिङ्-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, making an en-
closure, surrounding, encompassing; (अस्), m. the
plant Flacourtia Sapida.

वृत्ति, इस्, f. turning, turning round, revolving;
the circumference of a circle or wheel; being, ex-
istence, abiding (often at the end of comps., e. g.
तद्-वृत्ति, इस्, इस्, इ, abiding in that), staying, re-
maining; state, condition; proceeding, career, course
of conduct, conduct, behaviour, action (often at the
end of comps., cf. वक-व्˚); operation, practice,
business, profession, function, office, employment
[]
(at the end of comps. translatable by ‘employed
about,’ ‘engaged in’), mode of life [cf. वागुरा-
व्˚]; activity, cause or instrument of activity; treat-
ment, respectful treatment; livelihood, maintenance,
means of subsistence (often at the end of comps.,
cf. उञ्छ-व्˚; the means of subsistence for a
Brāhman are said in Manu IV. 4. to be, 1. ऋत,
‘true,’ i. e. lawful gleaning; 2. अ-मृत, ‘not deadly,’
i. e. unsolicited alms; 3. मृत, ‘deadly,’ i. e. soli-
cited alms; 4. प्र-मृत, ‘very deadly,’ i. e. agri-
culture; 5. सत्यानृत, ‘true and false,’ i. e. trade,
traffic; 6. श्व-वृत्ति, ‘dog-maintenance,’ i. e. servi-
tude; this last should never be engaged in, the preced-
ing two, i. e. agriculture and trade, only in times of
distress); wages, hire; customary allowance, perquisite,
fee; mode of thinking, course of ideas; style, force,
character, style in composition (especially dramatic
style, said to be of four kinds, viz. 1. Kaiśikī,
2. Bhāratī, 3. Sātvatī, 4. Ārabhaṭī, q. q. v. v.; the
first three are described as suited to the Śṛṅgāra,
Vīra, and Raudra Rasas respectively, the last as com-
mon to all); comment, commentary, explanation,
exposition, gloss; general character or force of a
word; (in grammar) a complex formation which
requires resolution or explanation (as distinguished
from a simple or uncompounded form, e. g. any
word formed with Kṛt or Taddhita affixes, any com-
pound and even duals and plurals which are regarded
as Dvandva compounds, of which only one member
is left, and all derivative verbs such as desideratives
&c.); a measure of the voice in reciting or chanting,
(of which, according to the Prātiśākhyas, there are
three, viz. वि-लम्बिता, मध्यमा, and द्रुता);
N. of a commentary by Sa-nandana.
—वृत्ति-कर्-
षित, अस्, आ, अम्, distressed for (want of) a liveli-
hood (Manu VIII. 411; according to Kullūka =
भृत्य्-अभावेन पीडितः).
—वृत्ति-च्छेद, अस्, m.
taking away the means of subsistence, confiscation
of a patrimony, deprivation of an hereditary office.
—वृत्ति-ता, f. or वृत्ति-त्व, अम्, n. state of being
or residing or being contained in, state of existence,
state, condition [cf. अनायत्त-व्˚]; mode of sub-
sistence, profession.
—वृत्ति-दान, अम्, n. the giving
of maintenance.
—वृत्ति-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing
means of subsistence; abiding; having a particular
way of thinking.
—वृत्ति-लाभ, अस्, m. discovery of
the concurrent (in phil.).
—वृत्ति-वैकल्य, अम्,
n. deficiency or lack of means of subsistence, want
of a livelihood.
—वृत्ति-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्, being in
any state or condition or employment; (अस्), m. a
chameleon (= सरट).
—वृत्ति-हेतु, उस्, m. cause
or means of subsistence.
—वृत्त्य्-अनुप्रास, अस्,
m. alliteration suited to any style or expression.
—वृत्त्य्-अर्थ-बोधक, अस्, इका, अम्, indicat-
ing the meaning of a complex formation, (see
under वृत्ति above.)
—वृत्त्य्-अर्थम्, ind. for the
sake of subsistence, in order to sustain life.
—वृत्त्य्-
उपाय, अस्, m. means of subsistence.

1. वृत्य, अस्, आ, अम्, (for 2. see p. 958, col. 1),
to be surrounded or encompassed, &c.; to be chosen,
eligible, preferable, excellent.

2. वृत्य, अस्, आ, अम् (for 1. see p. 956, col. 1),
to be abided or stayed or remained, &c.

वृत् 1. वृत् (for rt. 3. वृत् see p. 958,
col. 1), cl. 1. A. (in 2nd Fut., Aor., and
Cond. also P.; in Ved. and ep. P. also in other
forms) वर्तते (ep. वर्तति), Perf. ववृते (Ved.
वावृते, P. ववर्त), 2nd Fut. वर्तिष्यते and
वर्त्स्यति, Aor. अवर्तिष्ट and अवृतत्, Cond.
अवर्तिष्यत and अवर्त्स्यत् (Vedic forms [अनु]-
वर्त्ति, [आ] वर्त, अवर्त्, [सम्-आ] ववर्त्ति), वर्-
तितुम्, to turn, turn one's self, turn round, revolve,
roll, move, go; to move on, pass on, go on in
regular course, proceed, run a course, follow on; to
be or be situated in any particular manner or circum-
stances, to be, exist, live, subsist, remain, dwell, be
fixed, abide, stay, (मनसि or हृदये or हृदि
वृत्, to dwell or be turned over or thought over in
the mind, &c.); to be present; to take place, hap-
pen, come to pass; to conduce, tend to (with dat.);
to depend upon (with loc.); to occupy one's self,
employ one's self, be occupied or engaged in (with
loc., उपकारे वृत्, to give assistance); to behave,
demean one's self, act, practice, do, act towards
(with loc.), occupy one's self with (with inst.), act
in any particular manner (with inst., e. g. धर्मेण
वृत्, to act justly; अमायया वृत्, to act guilelessly;
व्याजेन वृत्, to act deceitfully); to enter upon a
particular course of conduct, act a part, (sometimes
with acc. वृत्तिम् added, e. g. वर्तसे वृत्तिम्
अक्षुद्राम्, thou art acting no mean part; यां
वृत्तिं वर्तामि पाण्डवेषु, whatever course I
enter upon towards the Pāṇḍavas): Pass. वृत्यते,
Aor. अवर्ति, &c., to be turned, &c.: Caus. वर्त-
यति, -ते, Aor. अवीवृतत्, अववर्तत्, to cause to
turn or revolve, cause to roll, cause to move or move
round, turn, move; to brandish (as a weapon); to
cause to move away, remove (Ved.); to shed (as
tears &c.); to cause to proceed, cause to be or exist,
make; to cause to take place, cause to pass (as
time), spend, pass, lead a life, live, (sometimes with
acc. वृत्तिम् added, or sometimes with inst. वृत्त्या
or वृत्तेन, or sometimes with inst. of other words,
e. g. भैक्षेण वर्तयति, he lives by begging);
to perform, practice, do, exhibit; to maintain one's
self, subsist (A.); to relate, recount, declare; to
perceive, comprehend; to care for (with dat.);
to read, study [cf. वृत्त]; (according to some) to
speak; to shine: Desid. विवर्तिषते and विवृत्-
सति, to wish to remain, desire to stay, &c.: Intens.
वरीवृत्यते, वरीवृतीति, वर्वृतीति, वरिवृतीति,
वर्वर्त्ति, वरिवर्त्ति, वरीवर्त्ति; [cf. Lat. vert-o,
versus; Goth. vairthan, ana-vairths, vaurs-tva;
Mod. Germ. werde, ward; Angl. Sax. weordhan,
ward, weard, wyrd; Lith. wartau, werciu, war-
toju, wirs-tu; Slav. vrat-i-ti.]

2. वृत्, त्, त्, त्, turning, turning round, moving,
existing; (त्), f., Ved. a turn, action, act, deed; (त्),
ind. ‘finished,’ a grammatical term signifying that a
series of roots acted on by a grammatical rule ends
with the word preceding वृत्.

वृत् 3. वृत्, cl. 4. A. वृत्यते (according
to others also cl. 1. वर्तते), to choose,
like, &c., generally used in an old Intens. form वा-
वृत्यते, (see वावृत्, which is classed by native
grammarians among simple roots.)

वृत्तक, अम्, n. a particular kind of prose com-
position.

वृत्र वृत्र, अस्, m. (probably fr. rt. वृ;
according to Uṇādi-s. II. 13. fr. rt. 1. वृत्), ‘the
coverer, hider, obstructer (of rain),’ N. of the Vedic
personification of an imaginary malignant influence
or demon of darkness and drought (supposed to take
possession of the clouds, causing them to obstruct
the clearness of the sky and keep back the waters;
Indra is represented as battling with this evil influ-
ence, and the pent up clouds being poetically pictured
as mountains or castles are shattered by his thunder-
bolt and made to open their receptacles; as a Dānava
or demon, Vṛtra is the son of Danu, q. v., and is
often associated with other evil spirits, such as Ahi,
[]
Śuṣṇa, Namuci, Pipru, Śambara, Uraṇa, whose
malignant influences are generally exercised in pro-
ducing darkness or drought); a cloud (in general);
darkness; a mountain; an enemy; sound, noise;
a wheel; N. of Indra (?); (अम्), n. a wicked person,
an enemy.
—वृत्र-खाद, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. ‘Vṛtra-
devouring,’ destroying Vṛtra; (अस्), m. a devourer
of enemies, epithet of Bṛhas-pati.
—वृत्र-घ्नी, f.,
N. of a river.
—वृत्र-तर, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. caus-
ing great darkness, (Sāy. = अतिशयेन लोकानाम् आव-
रकः or वृत्रैर् आवरणैः शत्रून् तरति यः,
i. e. overcoming enemies with darkness, Ṛg-veda I.
32, 5.)
—वृत्र-तुर्, ऊर्, m., Ved. ‘Vṛtra-conquer-
ing,’ epithet of Indra, conquering enemies (in gene-
ral).
—वृत्र-तूर्य, अम्, n., Ved. conquering
enemies, destruction of enemies; battle (= सङ्ग्रा-
म according to Naigh. II. 19).
—वृत्र-द्विष्, ट्,
m. ‘enemy of Vṛtra,’ epithet of Indra.
—वृत्र-
भोजन, अस्, m. a kind of pot-herb (commonly
called Samaṭh, described by some as a sort of cucum-
ber, = गण्डीर).
—वृत्र-वध, अस्, m. ‘the kill-
ing of Vṛtra,’ N. of the twenty-fifth and twenty-
sixth chapters of the Bhūmi-khaṇḍa of the Padma-
Purāṇa; of the seventy-ninth chapter of the Uttara-
kāṇḍa of the Rāmāyaṇa.
—वृत्र-शत्रु, उस्, m.
‘enemy of Vṛtra,’ epithet of Indra.
—वृत्र-हत्य,
अम्, आ, n. f., Ved. the slaying of Vṛtra, (Ṛg-veda VIII.
89, 5.)
—वृत्र-हथ, अस्, m., Ved. slaying Vṛtra,
slaying enemies.
—वृत्र-हन्, आ, m. ‘Vṛtra-killer,’
epithet of Indra; killer of enemies, victorious.
—वृ-
त्रहन्-तम, अस्, m., Ved. ‘most mighty slayer
of Vṛtra,’ epithet of Indra; a very victorious person.
—वृत्रारि (˚र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘enemy of Vṛtra,’ Indra.

वृत्त-वत्; add — round; having suitable occu-
pation.
